text: Designing a good REST API is like creating a clear map for other developers. First, your endpoints should be simple and logical, using nouns like `/users` or `/orders` instead of verbs. Always use proper HTTP status codes—for example, `200` for success, `404` when a resource is missing, and `400` for bad requests. This helps clients understand what happened without reading the response body. Next, never skip documentation. Even a short guide explaining each endpoint, its parameters, and expected responses saves hours of confusion. Finally, plan for versioning from the start. Add a version number to your URL (like `/v1/users`). This way, when you make breaking changes, old users still work while new users enjoy the updated features. A thoughtful API makes everyone’s life easier.
